public_rationale: The claim says Anthropic and OpenAI need venture money 'because their underlying businesses lose money on every transaction'. Read plainly, that means serving customers costs more than it earns. Anthropic's S-1 shows otherwise for the quarter before the post. In Q1 2026, revenue was $4,731 million and all compute and infrastructure costs, including research and training, were $3,387 million. Its cost of revenue was also well below revenue in 2025 ($2,773 million against $4,585 million) and in the first half of 2026. Anthropic did still run an operating loss in Q1 2026 and raised outside money, so its reliance on funding is not in doubt. But the stated cause fails for one of the two companies named. The $718 billion figure could not be verified, and OpenAI was not assessed.
limitations: Rests on Anthropic only; OpenAI's unit economics not reviewed.
The $718 billion commitment total is unverified.
Quarterly figures are unaudited; 'every transaction' is hyperbole read as negative gross margins.

statement.document_title: Am I Meant To Be Impressed?

from_speaker: "have promised $718 billion to Microsoft, Google and Amazon"
"because their underlying businesses lose money on every transaction"
our_interpretation: The causal core is that the companies depend on venture funding because their underlying business loses money on each sale. Plain reading of 'lose money on every transaction': the cost of serving customers exceeds the revenue from them, so gross margins are negative.
The period is the latest full quarter before the post, January to March 2026, since he describes a present state.
The $718 billion figure is his own tally of commitments; it is checked if evidence allows, but the outcome turns on the causal premise.
Contradicting the premise for either named company is enough to falsify a statement about both.
criteria.support_condition: Filings show that the cost of serving customers exceeded revenue (negative gross margin) in the period, so the companies needed outside capital to keep operating.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Filings show that revenue exceeded the cost of serving customers in the period, for example revenue greater than all compute spending, so the business does not lose money on each transaction.
